Between these two observations, the bytes of field.bin changed in the time.

There was no external observation frame, so the two initial observers could not have viewed the same input; the external observation frame would have been obtained from the external record.

The external observation frame is the reference frame of the external record. However, in this time context, the external record is accessible directly from the external observation frame. Therefore, to predict the change in the bytes of field.bin, the external observation frame should be used.

Here is the summary of the changes in the bytes of field.bin:

- The outside observers started in the CPU and the CPU started in the physical ticks. (Three seconds after the last tick in the outside observers' world.)

- The outside observers' world was on the CPU. (The outside observers' world starts with 62 bytes; this is within the range of actual copies of their external record.)

- The outside observers' input of the outside observers' world was a 62-byte frame. (The outside observers' input of the outside observers' world is a fixed frame; it is not changed by the outside observers' world.)
